name: Captain "Guegler"
summary: The captain Larry would call when he wanted off a remote site — his contact for the helicopter with call sign Rosethorn 007. Larry identifies him in uniform at the Huey in VN-0020: a man in his late fifties who had been in the military a long time, and who was always said to be a great pilot. On 2026-09-02 Larry placed him at the centre of the day his tour ended: it was this captain who flew up and took him off the mountain, dropping Sgt. Weaver off in his place, hours after the accusation about the "450 civilians" and around the time Larry believes he was reported killed in action.
researchNotes: SPELLING PROVENANCE, corrected 2026-09-02: of the five renderings held here, only "Geutler" is Larry's own. His son wrote it into the record as "captain Geutler (his spelling)" and confirmed afterwards that he had asked Larry directly and Larry spelled it that way. The other four are his son's transcriptions of the name as Larry says it, made at different times, and they should not be counted as independent evidence of how Larry renders the name — the archive has already made that mistake once with the base name, where four apparent renderings turned out to be one Larry spelling and three transcriptions. "Geutler" is therefore the first rendering with real evidentiary weight, and roster searches should lead with it. Remaining candidates to search alongside it: Guegler, Guetler, Gutler, Getler, Gugler, Geigler, Giegler, Kugler. A captain in his late fifties implies prior-enlisted or WWII/Korea service — a mustang profile that narrows roster searches usefully. Magnification (2026-08-15) settled an earlier tension: the tape once read as possibly beginning 'J' is the standard U.S. ARMY tape below aviator wings, so nothing in the photo contradicts the identification; his own name tape is hidden behind the jacket panel. The association with the erroneous killed-in-action report is no longer speculative in Larry's telling — he is the named pilot of the extraction on the last day — though nothing documentary yet ties him to the report itself.
